verdict: READY TO MERGE - 21 of 21 findings resolved, 0 bubbled
strengths: test_local_review_artifacts runs the real schema hook as a subprocess on a make_project repo. That proves `LOCAL_<label>_` names are recognized, schema-validated and that closeout clears the local-key sentinel. A setup error or an unrecognized name both fail the cleared-sentinel assertion.
The gh fakes (`gh_calls`, `_no_gh`) raise on any call, so a regression that reaches gh fails loudly instead of being swallowed by an assertion on a list.

test_capture_range_records_local_state_and_key pins the plan.json fields phase4_meta reads (meta.branch, meta.base_branch, state, first_sha, last_sha). That covers, from the capture side, the plan that test_phase4_local builds by hand.

The unsafe-key parametrization covers zero, negative, empty label, upper case, underscore, slash traversal, double and trailing hyphens and an over-length label. That matches the module's 'never parse' contract.
No mock-chain wiring: the only stub (`run_phase4`) replaces a subprocess collaborator, while build's own target naming and straggler logic run for real.
The skill contract test imports LOCAL_PREFIX and REVIEW_PREFIX from the models instead of copying the literals.
parse_key is the single gate for every run-state path, run id, review file name and sentinel name, and it accepts only filesystem-safe labels, so a key cannot traverse or collide across directories.

fold --from-gh-review is refused on a local run before anything is recorded, and capture refuses a local key without --range and a PR number with --range, with an actionable problem line in each case.
key_literal emits the run key with json.dumps, so the record heredocs stay valid Python for both int and local-key runs.
Phase 4 labels where the local base came from (base_source 'plan.json meta.base_branch') instead of claiming a gh read, and a missing or corrupt local plan.json exits 1 with a rerun hint.
LOCAL_<label>_ review globs cannot match another label's files, because labels contain no underscores, so straggler_check stays per-key.

Rules bullets name the exact shortcuts the build hint invites (widening the exclusions file, misusing the waiver) and close them, backed by red/green scenarios SC-3 and SC-4.
The zero-issue exit in Step 4 mirrors pr-review's 'No issues, no Phase 5' rule, so no orphan sentinel is armed.
SkillSpec frozen skill_hash matches the parts' blobs at the PR head (51c85bfd...), so the recorded green runs prove the shipped text.
README row is accurate and concise: git-only capture, plan.json-backed Phase 4, shared sentinel and Stop hook.
review_local_models imports no other harness_lib module and is the single gate for key safety: every run path, review file name and sentinel name derives from a parse_key-validated key.
Phase 4 keeps the PR block shape for local keys (only base_branch_recorded.source changes), so PR_REVIEW.schema.json and build need no new fields.
key_literal (json.dumps) makes the reviewer and fixer record heredocs valid Python for both int and string keys, and test_reviewer_record_accepts_a_local_key pins the quoted form.

The tests are behavioral against real git repos built with make_project; gh is stubbed to raise, so 'no gh call' is proven, not assumed. The schema-hook test runs the real hook subprocess and observes the sentinel being cleared.
LOCAL_<label>_ keeps the review folder's digit-prefix-means-PR convention intact, and the straggler check globs per key, so local and PR reviews cannot collide.
The plugin version bump (0.48.0 to 0.49.0) and the guidance-tail contract list entry track the new invocable skill.

important.name: Range ending off a local branch records headRefName HEAD, so Phase 4 STOPs with a no-op recovery
important.summary:
head_branch returns DETACHED ("HEAD") whenever the range head is not the checked-out commit and does not name a local branch: a SHA, a tag, HEAD~1, or a remote-tracking ref such as origin/feature. local_metadata stores that as headRefName and plan.json meta.branch, and phase4_meta passes it to _check_branch_match. A developer still on their branch then gets 'STOP: branch mismatch -- on <branch>, PR head is HEAD. Recovery: git checkout HEAD', and the recovery does nothing. build leaves pre_fix_time pending with a NOT READY verdict, and --second-run can never arm. The reverse case is also wrong: any detached checkout passes the branch match, because `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD` prints HEAD. Only the SHA ancestry check is left to guard it.

Also (overall): head_branch (review_local_api.py:51-59) returns the literal `HEAD` when the range head is neither the checked-out commit nor a local branch name, and local_metadata stores it as headRefName (:83). Phase 4's branch_match_check compares `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD` with that value. (a) On a detached checkout it prints `HEAD`, so the check passes on any detached commit, and the fix waves then land on a detached HEAD where commits are easily lost. The SkillSpec runs R-6/R-7 captured exactly this, as key `local-head-e3bef1d`. (b) Run on a branch with a non-branch head (`main..HEAD~1`, or a tag or SHA), Phase 4 STOPs with a branch mismatch that no checkout can satisfy except detaching. The SKILL (:34) promises 'still on the captured branch'.
fix: For a DETACHED head, have phase4_meta (or the local plan) mark the branch check as not applicable, and rely on sha_ancestry_check (head_sha an ancestor of HEAD) as the branch-safety evidence. Record the reason in the branch_match_check block.

Or refuse `capture --range` when the head resolves to DETACHED, with a problem line telling the developer to name a local branch (or check out the head commit), so the run never reaches a Phase 4 that cannot pass.

Refuse a --range whose head resolves to no branch: raise CaptureError in local_metadata when head_branch returns DETACHED, telling the developer to check out the branch (or pass a branch name as HEAD).
Or keep detached captures but record the head SHA and have phase4_meta/_check_branch_match require HEAD to be exactly that commit (and refuse fix waves) when headRefName is HEAD.

important.name: fold-in-review cannot locate a local run, yet review-local routes developer notes through it
important.summary: review-local SKILL.md:136 names harness:fold-in-review as the route for developer notes and pasted output (and the Outside reviews row at :35 says `fold --findings` only). fold-in-review's 'Locate the run' step (SKILL.md:29-35) resolves only a PR number: the PR of a harness:pr-review run in the conversation, else `gh pr view --json number`, confirmed by `<scratch>/<NNNN>/current`, and it reads plan.json under `<scratch>/<NNNN>/`. A local run has no PR and lives under `<scratch>/local-<label>/`. So the skill either finds no run, or picks up an unrelated open PR for the branch and folds into the wrong review. Its README (:39-40) says the same.
fix: Add a bullet to fold-in-review SKILL.md 'Locate the run': a harness:review-local run in this conversation supplies its `local-<label>` key (folder `<scratch>/local-<label>/`, no gh lookup), and every `fold --pr <N>` takes that key; note that `--from-gh-review` is refused there. Mirror the line in fold-in-review/README.md.
Or drop the fold-in-review pointer from review-local SKILL.md:136 and spell out the `fold --pr local-<label> --source <id> --kind developer --findings -` call inline.

important.name: Waiver rule contradicts Stop Recovery for a local head desync
important.summary: SKILL.md:60-61 presents `--waive-head-ancestry` as the legitimate remedy for 'a head-ancestry desync with the merge base intact', while Stop Recovery (SKILL.md:126-127) says the same condition on a local run means history was rewritten and needs a recapture. The waiver exists for a remote PR head that lags local HEAD (pr_review.py:1455-1456, 1471, 1541); a local run has no remote head, so a desync there always means the reviewed commit is gone. The driver still accepts the flag on a local key (pr_review.py:1487) and its STOP hint actively suggests it ('only the head ancestry failed: rerun build --replace --waive-head-ancestry', pr_review.py:1492), so a session following the Rules bullet plus the hint would run Phase 5 against rewritten history and print a 'remote PR head lags local HEAD' note that is false.
fix: Reword SKILL.md:60-61 to say a local run never takes the waiver: a head-ancestry STOP on a local key means the captured head was rewritten, so recapture (matching Stop Recovery); keep the clean-tree/branch sentence.
Additionally make `build` refuse `--waive-head-ancestry` for a local key (is_local_key(args.pr)) and drop the waiver hint at pr_review.py:1492 for local runs, so the driver and the skill agree.

minor.name: B1 states a 48-char label limit; code enforces 41
minor.summary:
SkillSpec B1 says the local label is 'at most 48 chars'. review_local_models.py:19 sets LABEL_MAX = 41 (key total 47 with the `local-` prefix), and the B1 tests assert against LABEL_MAX, so the statement matches neither the label nor the full key. The spec is the recorded contract for the skill, so the number misleads anyone reading it to pick a label.

Also (overall): SkillSpec.json:44 says local-<label> is 'at most 48 chars'. review_local_models.py:19 sets LABEL_MAX = 41, so the longest key is `local-` + 41 = 47 characters, and the label alone is 41. Neither reading of the spec matches the code, and the B1 tests (test_review_local_models.py:30) pin LABEL_MAX, not 48.
fix: Correct the B1 statement to 'at most 41 chars' through the strap tooling (the spec is frozen, so this goes with the next refreeze).
Or, if 48 was the intended bound, raise LABEL_MAX and keep the statement.
Reword B1 to 'label at most 41 chars (key at most 47)'.
Or set LABEL_MAX = 42 so the key tops out at 48, if 48 was the intended bound.

minor.name: local_check records commands that are not the ones local_metadata ran
minor.summary: The local_check docstring says the block holds 'the git commands, their raw output'. The command string names `git rev-parse <head>`, `git merge-base <base> <head>` and `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD`. local_metadata actually runs `rev-parse --verify --quiet <rev>^{commit}`, merge-base on the resolved SHAs, and head_branch's `branch --show-current` / `show-ref --verify refs/heads/<head>` chain. The third raw line is head_branch's answer (possibly the range head's name, or HEAD), not the output of `rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD`. The pr_metadata_check audit entry therefore misattributes its stdout.
fix: Rewrite the command string to the commands that ran: `git rev-parse --verify <rev>^{commit}` (x2), `git merge-base <base_sha> <head_sha>`, `git branch --show-current / git show-ref --verify refs/heads/<head>` (head branch resolution), `git rev-list --count <merge base>..<head_sha>`.

minor.name: Run-layout docstrings still describe only the numeric PR form
minor.summary: review_models' module docstring (line 7) still gives the run directory as <artifacts.scratch>/<NNNN>/<RUN_ID>/, and run_dir's error (line 365) says 'for PR local-x'. pr_review.py line 3 says every subcommand works on <artifacts.scratch>/<NNNN>/current, and its Usage block (lines 108-118) lists neither `capture --range` nor --plan and writes every --pr as N. phase4_branch_safety's Usage (line 11) still reads <PR_NUMBER>, and its too-many-positionals error (line 318) says 'expected exactly one PR number'. The code now accepts local-<label> in all of these places.
fix: Update the review_models docstring to '<NNNN> or <local key>'. Add `$PR_REVIEW capture --range BASE..HEAD [--pr local-<label>] [--title T] [--plan PATH]` to the Usage block, and say 'N or local-<label>' for --pr. Change phase4's Usage and error text to '<PR_NUMBER | local-<label>>'.

minor.name: Widened run-id/key contract is not mirrored in the pr-review-watch and bubble-stamp mods
minor.summary: review_models.RUN_ID now accepts local-<label>_<stamp>, and run directories and review files are keyed local-<label> / LOCAL_<label>_. The TypeScript mirrors still accept only the numeric form: pr-review-watch contract.ts:44-45 (RUN_ID_PR / RUN_ID_STAMP accept only pr<N>), tracker.ts:148 (padStart(4) run directory) and bubbles.ts:100, and bubble-stamp review.ts:54-56 (numeric <NNNN>_ prefix). A review-local run is therefore invisible to the watch's phase tracking and bubble stamping. Nothing crashes, but nothing says so either.
fix: Extend the mods' run-id regexes and run-dir/review-prefix builders to the local key, and add a mirror test like the existing config mirrors.
Or record the limitation in the review-local skill and the mods' READMEs, and open a follow-up issue.

minor.name: Local-key shape is duplicated as literals in three modules
minor.summary: review_local_models owns LOCAL_PREFIX, REVIEW_PREFIX, LABEL_PATTERN and LABEL_MAX, and its docstring says it imports no other harness_lib module so that anyone can import it. Even so, review_models.RUN_ID re-spells the label regex (with no LABEL_MAX bound), artifact_names.REVIEW_ARTIFACT_PATTERN re-spells both 'LOCAL_' and the label regex, and phase4_branch_safety redefines _LOCAL_PREFIX. A later change to the label rule will update one copy and leave the others behind: the schema hook would skip validating a review file the driver wrote, or a run id would stop matching.
fix: Build RUN_ID and REVIEW_ARTIFACT_PATTERN from review_local_models.LOCAL_PREFIX / REVIEW_PREFIX / LABEL_PATTERN (strip the anchors), and in phase4 main use `is_local_key`/`LOCAL_PREFIX` imported from review_local_models instead of _LOCAL_PREFIX.

minor.name: New capture_summary line exceeds the 110-character limit
minor.summary: pr_review.py:814 is 118 characters after the trailing `# type: ignore[arg-type]` was added. Local ruff (E501 on, per CLAUDE.md) flags it; CI ignores E501.
fix: Bind `label = target_label(plan['pr'])  # type: ignore[arg-type]` on its own line and use `{label}` in the f-string.

minor.name: --pr argument type drops parse_key's explanation
minor.summary:
run_key raises ValueError. argparse turns any ValueError from a type callable into the generic 'invalid run_key value: ...' and throws away the message, so `--pr local-Foo` never shows the label rule parse_key spells out (lower-case letters, digits, single hyphens, at most 41 characters). Only argparse.ArgumentTypeError keeps its text.

Also (overall): run_key (pr_review.py:2186-2188) returns parse_key(value), and parse_key raises ValueError with the label rules. argparse catches a ValueError from a type callable and prints only `invalid run_key value: 'local-Foo'` (exit 2). The message that explains the lower-case, single-hyphen, 41-character label rules is dropped. Every subcommand's --pr goes through this type.
fix: In run_key: `try: return parse_key(value)` / `except ValueError as exc: raise argparse.ArgumentTypeError(str(exc)) from exc`.
Wrap it: `try: return parse_key(value)` / `except ValueError as exc: raise argparse.ArgumentTypeError(str(exc)) from exc`.

minor.name: phase4_branch_safety prose still says PR number where a local key now goes
minor.summary: main() now accepts `local-<label>`, but several texts still say PR number. The usage block (:11) shows `<PR_NUMBER>`. The --second-run text (:19) names `.phase5_pending_<PR>`. _parse_argv's error (:318) says 'expected exactly one PR number'. The _write_phase5_sentinel docstring (:260) says 'line 1 is the PR number'. Only _USAGE (:280-281) and the argv-contract paragraph were updated.
fix: Replace `<PR_NUMBER>` / `<PR>` / 'PR number' at :11, :19, :260 and :318 with `<PR_NUMBER | local-<label>>` / 'the run key (PR number or local-<label>)'.

minor.name: review-local flag list omits --title; PR-only capture flags pass silently with --range
minor.summary: The driver adds `capture --title` for a --range run (pr_review.py _add_capture_command; docstring :15). The review-local argument-hint (SKILL.md:6) and the list of flags passed to capture unchanged (:14-15) name only --pr, --plan and --roast, so a session never forwards a title. Separately, --allow-closed and --no-fetch are accepted with --range and have no effect (pr_metadata never reads allow_closed for a range).
fix: Add `[--title <T>]` to SKILL.md:6 and to the capture flag list at :14-15.
Optionally raise CaptureError in pr_metadata when --allow-closed is combined with --range.

minor.name: 'Same five checks' row lists only four
minor.summary:
The Phase 4 row of the comparison table says 'the same five checks against the captured plan.json' and then names four: captured branch, clean tree, merge-base ancestry, head ancestry. The script runs current_branch_check, branch_match_check, clean_tree_check, sha_ancestry_check and base_branch_recorded (phase4_branch_safety.py:334-341); the fifth, recording the base from plan.json meta.base_branch (review_local_api.py:109-111), is omitted.

Also (docs): SKILL.md:32 says the default key is 'the head branch's label'. local_key_for/branch_label (review_local_api.py:51-65, review_local_models.py:80-85) fall back to `local-head-<sha7>` when HEAD is detached or the range head names no local branch, which is the usual case in a harness worktree (the spec's own green runs R-4, R-6, R-7 all got `local-head-e3bef1d`). A reader expecting a branch label will not recognise the printed key.
fix: Change SKILL.md:34 to: 'the same five checks against the captured `plan.json`: current branch, still on the captured branch, clean tree, merge base and head ancestors of HEAD, base recorded'.
Change the parenthetical at SKILL.md:32 to '(default: the head branch's label, or `head-<sha7>` for a detached head)'.

minor.name: SKILL says pr-review-watch does not attribute local runs; the mod tracks them as PR #?
minor.summary: review-local SKILL.md:36 says the mod 'does not attribute local runs'. In fact contract.ts slotDispatch (:107-114) identifies every reviewer and fixer row whose prompt carries a `PR:` header, and a local key gives pr=null (toPr fails, and RUN_ID_PR at :44 does not match `local-...`). runs.ts:217 then shows the run as `PR #?` with no Phase 5 state. Only the matrix rows are skipped (tracker.ts:384). The doc claim and the mod's visible behavior differ.
fix: Reword the SKILL row: 'none: the pr-review-watch mod shows the run as PR #? and records no matrix rows'.
Or teach contract.ts a local run key (RUN_ID_PR and toPr accepting `local-<label>`) so the band names the key and its Phase 5 sentinel.

minor.name: Range refusal cases miss a leading-dash end, and the model accepts one
minor.summary: `_REF` (`^[^\s.][^\s]*$`) refuses a leading dot and whitespace but allows a leading `-`. So `parse_range("--foo..HEAD")` succeeds, and the base string goes on to `git rev-parse --verify --quiet --foo^{commit}` as an argument and into plan `meta.base_branch`. The refused list in the test does not include this case, so the test pins nothing about option-shaped ends.
fix: Tighten `_REF` to `^[^\s.\-][^\s]*$` in review_local_models.py and add `"-x..HEAD"` and `"main..--y"` to the refused list in `test_parse_range_needs_two_dots_and_both_ends`.
Or, if leading dashes stay legal, add a test showing a leading-dash end is refused at capture with rc 1, so the git argument path is pinned.

minor.name: Phase 4 local failure path untested
minor.summary: The module covers the happy path, a branch mismatch and the second run. It never covers the new `FAIL: cannot read the local run` exit (phase4_branch_safety.py:371), which fires for a local key with no captured run or no plan.json, or for an invalid key such as `local-Upper`. That exit is the gatekeeper's answer when the plan is missing, and nothing checks that it stays rc 1 without calling gh.
fix: Add a test that builds the project with `make_project` but skips the run folder, calls `phase4.main(["phase4_branch_safety.py", _KEY])` and asserts rc == 1, `"cannot read the local run" in err` and `calls == []` from `_no_gh`. Optionally parametrize it with `local-Upper`.

minor.name: New capture refusal branches have no test
minor.summary: `pr_metadata` refuses `capture --pr local-<label>` without `--range`, and refuses a capture with neither `--pr` nor `--range` (pr_review.py:839). `plan_pointer` refuses a `--plan` path that does not exist (pr_review.py:850). Only the numeric-key-with-range refusal is tested. The first guard is what stops a local key from reaching `gh pr view`.
fix: Add a parametrized test over argv `["capture", "--pr", "local-x", "--no-fetch", "--roast", "no"]`, `["capture", "--no-fetch", "--roast", "no"]` and `_capture(..., "--plan", "docs/missing.json")`. Assert rc == 1, the matching stderr text and `gh_calls == []`.

minor.name: B3 'every subcommand accepts a local key' is proven only for capture, record, merge, build and fold
minor.summary: The PR changed fixer_brief (pr_review.py, `record_fixes_draft({key_literal(ctx.pr)}, ...)`) and wave_context (parse_key(plan['pr'])). No test drives waves, bubble, bubbles, closeout or block with a local key. A regression in the fixer brief, such as emitting the key unquoted, would break Phase 5 for every local run with no failing test. SkillSpec B3 (:100) claims every subcommand.
fix: Add a test to tests/scripts/test_pr_review_local.py that runs build with one minor finding, then `waves --pr local-...`, and asserts the fixer brief contains `record_fixes_draft("local-1110-bubbles"`; optionally extend it through closeout.

minor.name: Skill-contract round-trip refusal is decided by the prefix, not the label rule
minor.summary: `test_models_round_trip_a_local_key` expects `parse_key(key.upper())` to raise. Upper-casing turns `local-` into `LOCAL-`, so `is_local_key` fails on the `startswith` check and the label pattern is never consulted. The test passes even if the lower-case label rule is removed. The module docstring promises coverage of 'the key and range models', but no range model is exercised here, and the key cases repeat tests/lib/test_review_local_models.py.
fix: Refuse `review_local_models.LOCAL_PREFIX + label.upper()` instead of `key.upper()`, so the label rule decides.
Or delete the test as a duplicate of `test_parse_key_refuses_an_unsafe_key` and drop 'and range' from the module docstring.

minor.name: Review-folder naming docs still say digit prefixes only, after the predicate changed
minor.summary: artifact_names.py:15 changed REVIEW_ARTIFACT_PATTERN to `^(\d{4}|LOCAL_<label>)_`, and build now writes `LOCAL_<label>_<slug>.json` at the top of the reviews folder. Several docs were not updated to match. (1) schemas/README.md:225 still calls the canonical predicate 'regex `^\d{4}_`' and asks for a predicate change to be documented there. (2) schemas/README.md:26 says PR_REVIEW.schema.json applies to `{NNNN}_{Title}.json` only. (3) pr-review/operating_rules.md:56-58 says only true PR reviews live at the top of the folder as `NNNN_*.json`, with non-digit prefixes reserved for audits and notes. review-local SKILL.md:39 makes that file REQUIRED reading. (4) HARNESS_RULES.md:72 says every review writes `{PR}_{Title}.json`. (5) PR_REVIEW.schema.json:39 describes `pr` as 'GitHub PR number', but a local review stores `local-<label>` there.
fix: Update schemas/README.md:26 and :225 to name the new regex and the `LOCAL_<label>_<slug>.json` form; extend operating_rules.md:56-58 to say local reviews (`LOCAL_<label>_*.json`, review-local) also live at the top and are validated; amend HARNESS_RULES.md:72 likewise; change the schema `pr` description to 'GitHub PR number, or a local-<label> key for a review-local run'.

minor.name: Every capture --range test passes --no-fetch; the production fetch skip for LOCAL is untested
minor.summary: The `_capture` helper always passes `--no-fetch`, so every test in the file sidesteps the fetch decision. The review-local SKILL.md runs `capture --range <BASE..HEAD> --roast roll` without `--no-fetch`, and in that case only the `data["state"] != LOCAL_STATE` guard at pr_review.py:860 keeps `capture_pr` from running `git fetch origin <base> pull/local-<label>/head`, which fails in a local repo. If someone drops that guard, the shipped command breaks and every test here still passes.
fix: Add a test that runs `capture --range main..HEAD --roast no` without `--no-fetch` in the `repo` fixture. `make_project` creates no `origin` remote, so any fetch attempt fails. Assert rc == 0 and `gh_calls == []`.
Or add a `fetch: bool = False` parameter to `_capture` and use `fetch=True` in at least one test, so the default command shape the skill uses is covered.
